messages:
maria: Heads up — infra CI failing on gpu-nodepool scale in eu-west1. terraform apply aborts with 'no matching nodepool label for selector'. Looks like new nodes join but labels aren't present, so the k8s nodeSelector match in our module fails. Anyone seen this?
deploy-bot: [CI] run 38912 - infra/terraform (apply) failed on job `scale-gpu-pool` — exit code 1. Logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/runs/38912
chris: I hit this locally too. Autoscaler created instances but kubelet shows nodes without the label `workload.gpu/type: a100`. The instance-template includes the label in cloud-init but node never gets it.
jen: This started after the runner-autoscaler TTL change merged yesterday (PR #1245). Could be the node comes up and gets tainted/cordoned before the k8s join hook runs? :thinking_face:
sean: Quick grep of the join logs from one of the failed nodes: 
```
kubeadm join ... --discovery-token-unsafe-skip-ca-verification
ubuntu@node: systemd[1]: cloud-init.service: Succeeded.
[setup] applying labels from /etc/node-labels.yaml
ERROR: cannot apply label workload.gpu/type=a100: node not found
```
Seems like the label apply script runs before the node registers with the control plane. Timing race.
chris: Also noticed GH Actions cache/restore sometimes speeds up the workflow steps a lot — that could shave off a few seconds from join -> kubelet start ordering and push us into the race window. Might explain why CI flakes but infra runs fine in other contexts.
maria: Repro steps I used: trigger job with matrix target=eu-west1, machine-type=n1-standard-32, scale count 3. Terraform plan succeeds, apply fails during module `k8s.nodepool.module`. Full error: 
```
Error: No matching nodes found for selector: label "workload.gpu/type" not present on any node
```
jen: For quick mitigation can we add a retry-wait in the TF null_resource that runs `kubectl get nodes -l workload.gpu/type -o name` with a 30s backoff? Ugly but buy time while we root cause.
infra-sre: I'd rather avoid terraform polling. Safer fix: modify the node boot script to loop until kubelet has registered before writing labels. Small patch in cloud-init: wait-for-node-registration.sh. I'll draft.
chris: Another option: change autoscaler to attach labels via instance metadata, then use a controller that patches node once it appears. But we risk duplicate agents and more complexity.
sean: For a short-term CI workaround we can add a pre-check step in GH Actions: `kubectl get nodes -l workload.gpu/type` with a retry until count matches expected. If not, fail fast and queue a retry. That avoids terraform being stuck in partial state.
maria: Can someone revert the TTL change to autoscaler while we investigate? That PR indeed landed last night and correlated with spike in these errors. Revert would reduce churn.
jen: I opened a revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1253 — links to the failure runs in the description.
deploy-bot: CI: revert PR 1253 triggered — preview run 38928 created.
infra-sre: I'm prepping a minimal cloud-init patch to gate label application on node presence. Patch will be small, will post here in a minute.
chris: Also adding a tiny `sleep 10` is brittle. Do the proper loop: `until kubectl get node "$HOSTNAME"; do sleep 5; done` then apply labels.
maria: OK plan: 1) Merge revert PR 1253 (jen) 2) Add cloud-init patch (infra-sre) 3) Add pre-check retry step in GH Actions (sean/chris) 4) Open post-mortem ticket and track root cause.
infra-sre: Created ticket INFRA-4321: "autoscaler/TTL race causes node label propagation failure during node join" — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4321
jen: Revert merged. We'll monitor CI for a couple runs. Please comment on INFRA-4321 with any logs.
chris: After revert + cloud-init patch, I'll run a stress test (50 nodepool scales) in staging to validate.
maria: Thanks everyone. Marking this thread resolved for now — follow up in INFRA-4321. :thumbsup:
